subject: Business Models
title: Medieval Guilds
description: A micro-lesson that makes Medieval Guilds usable.

hook.text: In medieval Europe, you couldn't just open a shop. You needed permission from the guild.

buildup.text: Guilds controlled who could practice a trade, set prices, and enforced quality standards.

discovery.text: Apprentices trained for 7+ years before becoming masters. The guild was school, union, and regulator.

twist.text: Guilds also blocked innovation. New techniques threatened existing members, so they were often banned.

climax.text: Guilds eventually lost power as markets grew beyond local control. Free trade won.

punchline.text: Quality control or cartel? Guilds were both.

quiz.question: How long did guild apprenticeships typically last?

details.summary: Medieval guilds were associations of craftsmen and merchants that controlled training, quality standards, pricing, and market access in European cities from the 11th to 16th centuries..
details.whyItMatters: Guilds invented quality control, professional training through apprenticeships, and industry self-regulation. Modern trade associations, professional licensing.
takeaways: Guilds controlled training via apprenticeship, quality standards, and market access
They functioned as monopolies that limited competition and fixed prices in cities
Modern professional licensing and industry standards descend from guild practices

faq.question: How did the guild apprenticeship system work?
faq.answer: Boys aged 12 to 14 entered 5 to 7 year apprenticeships with master craftsmen. After apprenticeship, they became journeymen who traveled to work under different masters. To become a master and open their own shop, they had to produce a masterpiece approved by existing guild masters.

faq.question: Why did guilds eventually lose their power?
faq.answer: The rise of factory production made individual craft skills less relevant. Enlightenment economics argued against monopolistic controls. Nation-states consolidated regulatory power away from local guilds..
